sources.title: Emdash README
sources.locator: Overview, setup, features and component boundaries
sources.finding: Classic runs installed coding CLIs in parallel Git worktrees on local or SSH machines. README lists desktop installers for macOS/Windows/Linux and Apache-2.0, with PR/check/merge workflow and separate provider data handling.

sources.title: Emdash license
sources.finding: The cited root license governs this repository distribution, subject to component notices.

sources.title: Emdash Tasks
sources.locator: Creating a Task; Worktrees; After Starting
sources.finding: Tasks select branches, issues or PRs, choose an agent and create a worktree by default. Existing workspaces and root checkout are also available.

sources.title: Emdash Providers
sources.locator: Supported Providers; Feature Support; Remote agents
sources.finding: Names 35 detected CLI integrations, with provider-specific hooks, resume and model/effort options; remote CLIs must be installed and authenticated remotely.

sources.title: Emdash Automations
sources.finding: Cron prompts run on the project machine. The remote Workspace Server schedules without a connected desktop, except steps needing desktop services. Runs link to tasks and expose errors.

sources.title: Emdash Telemetry
sources.locator: Summary; Opt Out; What We Collect
sources.finding: Production telemetry defaults on, uses allowlisted PostHog events, can attach account identity after sign-in, and has settings/environment opt-out.

sources.title: Emdash Remote Development
sources.finding: The remote Workspace Server handles repos, agents, terminals and scheduling over SSH; local credentials are not automatically copied.

sources.title: Emdash Tmux Sessions
sources.finding: Optional tmux retains terminal/TUI processes across app disconnects, but not reboot. Local Windows sessions do not use tmux.

sources.title: Emdash Diff View
sources.finding: Documents file staging, diffs and Git workflow actions.

sources.title: Emdash CI/CD Checks
sources.finding: Shows GitHub check status; this does not establish enforced delivery gates.

sources.title: Emdash Library
sources.finding: Reusable prompts, skills and MCP configuration are managed in the Library.

sources.title: Emdash Roadmap
sources.finding: Roadmap points to discussions and issue requests, rather than a dated delivery commitment.

sources.title: Emdash desktop build
sources.finding: The documented desktop client uses Electron.

sources.title: Emdash in-app browser
sources.finding: Task browser previews can forward remote ports and restore saved tabs/profiles. It does not reuse system-browser profiles or extensions.

sources.title: Emdash Classic
sources.finding: The Emdash Classic page answers that Emdash is open source and free to use. This covers the application, not agent subscriptions or remote machine costs.

sources.title: Emdash Where to find it; Actions; Inline editing
sources.locator: Where to find it; Actions; Inline editing
sources.finding: Classic updates changed/staged files from workspace Git events and offers unified/split diffs, inline editing of unstaged files, stage/unstage/discard, commit, push and create PR. Discard asks confirmation. PR views show files, commits, checks, comments and merge state; GitHub account/remote required for PR operations.

sources.title: Emdash Viewing checks; Refreshing check runs; Requirements
sources.locator: Viewing checks; Refreshing check runs; Requirements
sources.finding: Checks display pass/fail/pending/skipped, source, timing and links for the PR current head commit; opening Checks or a new head refreshes GitHub data. PR comments appear below checks. Requires a selected GitHub account, PR and configured checks.

sources.title: Emdash Library sections
sources.finding: Library saves reusable prompts for new or existing conversations, installs/creates skills and configures MCP servers. Remote configuration is scoped to that machine and is not automatically copied from the laptop.

sources.title: Emdash Create an automation; Review runs
sources.finding: Scheduled runs select name, project, cron, prompt, agent and workspace. History shows timing, status and errors with associated task/conversation links. Runs can become regular tasks. Pausing stops future schedules.

sources.title: Emdash Supported providers; Feature support; Remote agents
sources.locator: Supported providers; Feature support; Remote agents
sources.finding: Classic names Pi and Grok among its 35 CLI providers. Auto-approve skips file-operation permission prompts for the providers that support it; resume/hooks vary by provider. Credentials and installation must exist on the execution machine; per-agent/machine model and effort preferences are remembered.

sources.title: Emdash homepage
sources.locator: Hero and 'All your coding agents in one place'; 'Get early access' form
sources.finding: Emdash 2.0 is an early-access team product that runs agents on the user's infrastructure or Emdash cloud with the user's own subscriptions and models; no prices are shown.

sources.title: Emdash Claude Code auth status check
sources.locator: packages/plugins/src/agents/impl/claude/auth.ts lines 17-33 and 46-56 (claudeAuthStatus, accountFromAuthStatus), release v1.2.11 commit 9346e91
sources.finding: Emdash treats Claude Code as authenticated when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set or when the installed claude CLI reports a signed-in account through its own auth status, including an OAuth account; Emdash holds no model credentials of its own.

sources.title: Emdash Providers docs
sources.locator: Supported Providers, Remote agents and Adding a Provider sections (last updated 2026-10-17)
sources.finding: Emdash detects installed provider CLIs on PATH; some CLIs need their own account authentication before Emdash can run them, and on remote machines the user installs and authenticates the CLI there.

sources.title: Emdash Antigravity support at v1.2.11
sources.finding: Emdash Classic v1.2.11 detects agy or antigravity and builds runnable Antigravity commands with initial prompts, models, permission flags and conversation resume.
